Package neqsim.process.util.optimizer

Class ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeLifecycleStudy

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.util.optimizer.ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeLifecycleStudy
public final class ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeLifecycleStudy extends Object
Aggregates independently validated accepted-point envelope studies across ordered lifecycle periods.

Every period is admitted only through ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeStudy.getAcceptedPointEnvelopeEvidence(String, OperatingPointSearchResult, SliceResult...), so a lifecycle report cannot bypass accepted-point replay, finite-candidate, complete-constraint, restoration, or slice-completion checks. Periods must use the same ordered action identifiers, but may use independently configured process models, constraints, equipment availability and operating limits. This keeps lifecycle comparison separate from the physical models that own those definitions.

The result reports sampled accepted bottleneck changes between adjacent periods. It is advisory evidence, not a continuous forecast, equipment qualification, shadow price, operating approval, or substitute for period-specific convergence and constraint evidence.

      public ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeLifecycleStudy addPeriod(String periodId, String periodName, double elapsedTime, String configurationProvenance, ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeStudy study, ProcessModelOperatingPointOptimizer.OperatingPointSearchResult search, ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeStudy.SliceResult... slices)
      Adds one completely validated period in strictly increasing elapsed-time order.

      The process/evaluator may differ between periods, allowing reservoir state, equipment availability, operating limits and qualified map inputs to change. The ordered action identifiers must remain identical so accepted operating vectors retain a stable meaning. The source study performs all model-state and envelope validation before this method mutates the lifecycle builder.

      Parameters:
      periodId - unique stable period identifier
      periodName - human-readable period name
      elapsedTime - non-negative elapsed time from the lifecycle origin
      configurationProvenance - period-specific reservoir, availability and operating-limit basis
      study - exact runtime envelope study
      search - accepted mixed operating-point search from the same evaluator
      slices - one or more complete accepted-point slices from the same study
      Returns:
      this study

      Adds one completely validated period together with accepted physical-state evidence.

      State metrics describe the independently accepted reservoir, network, host, or shared-resource state used to define this period. Metric identifiers, ordering, and units must remain identical across every period. Values must be finite. This method does not rerun or qualify the source physical model; callers must supply only values from an already accepted state and retain that source in each metric's provenance.

      Parameters:
      periodId - unique stable period identifier
      periodName - human-readable period name
      elapsedTime - non-negative elapsed time from the lifecycle origin
      configurationProvenance - period-specific reservoir, availability and operating-limit basis
      acceptedStateMetrics - ordered accepted physical-state metrics
      study - exact runtime envelope study
      search - accepted mixed operating-point search from the same evaluator
      slices - one or more complete accepted-point slices from the same study
      Returns:
      this study

    • getPeriodChangeDiagnostics

      public List<Map<String,Object>> getPeriodChangeDiagnostics()
      Reports exact sampled changes between each pair of adjacent lifecycle periods.

      Diagnostics compare accepted action values and slices with identical ordered action axes. Points are comparable only when their physical axis-value vectors are exactly equal. Added or removed grids remain explicit rather than being interpolated. The diagnostics therefore describe only the sampled evidence and do not infer a continuous envelope boundary or causal constraint change.

      Returns:
      deeply immutable ordered period-change diagnostics

    • toEvidenceJson

      public String toEvidenceJson(String cycleId)
      Serializes lifecycle evidence for the continuous-task proposal boundary.

      Unlike the general map export, this handoff requires the current living-task cycle to be one of the independently validated lifecycle periods. The selected period's envelope therefore already carries the same cycle identifier, allowing the downstream production guard to bind the optimizer replay, accepted envelope and lifecycle evidence without rewriting model-produced JSON.

      Parameters:
      cycleId - current living-task cycle identifier and lifecycle period identifier
      Returns:
      compact JSON containing exact schema-v8, installed-coverage schema-v9, plant-coverage schema-v11, qualified paired-relief schema-v12, ranked paired-relief schema-v13, joint-relief schema-v14, paired-envelope schema-v15, or sampled-cell paired-envelope schema-v16 evidence
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the current cycle is not an accepted lifecycle period

    • constraintSummaryIdentityEvidence

      private static List<Map<String,Object>> constraintSummaryIdentityEvidence(ProcessModelOperatingEnvelopeLifecycleStudy.PeriodEvidence period)
      Extracts exact rejecting or near-active identity rows from one accepted period summary.

      Rank, occurrence counts, headroom, and representative evidence are intentionally excluded. The retained identity contains the classification and complete engineering basis, so a change between NEAR_ACTIVE and REJECTING, a changed applicable limit, or changed provenance appears as one removed and one added identity.

      Parameters:
      period - accepted lifecycle period
      Returns:
      immutable exact identity rows in summary rank order
